predecessors.note: Bashu and Hanzhong were Qin land; Xiang Yu enfeoffed Liu Bang with them when he created the Eighteen Kingdoms in 206 (Eighteen Kingdoms table: Hàn 漢, Liu Bang, 'Sichuan, Chongqing, southern Shaanxi').

successors.note: 'In 202 BC, Liu became emperor with the support of his subjects' (Gaozu page). The Han dynasty is the same state under a new title; Cliopatria's Han Dynasty row begins in 202. The dossier ends on 28 February 202 (fx-39, R009), the day Liu Bang becomes emperor; the Han dynasty starts in the same year.

capitals.note: 'In 205 BC, Liu designated his son Liu Ying as crown prince and stationed him in Yueyang.' The page calls no city the capital in these years; Luoyang and then Chang'an are the capitals after 202 (undated there).

correction.text: Liu Bang's kingdom at its grant in 206: 'Sichuan, Chongqing, southern Shaanxi' (Eighteen Kingdoms)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 206 only: the grant is Bashu and Hanzhong, 'Sichuan, Chongqing, southern Shaanxi' (the table's words, Eighteen Kingdoms page re-read 2026-10-19). Revised 2026-10-19: the first draft drew Bashu as the whole Sichuan region (2,328 cells, 740 of them west of 102.5 E on the Ganzi/Aba plateau, outside both Cliopatria Han shapes), which made the grant (2,425 cells) larger than Cliopatria's whole 206 shape (2,341 cells: Sichuan 1,121, Henan 377, Shaanxi 313, Chongqing 273, Gansu 166) - the note's 'far larger' was wrong. The grant is now the Cliopatria Han cells inside the Sichuan region (Sichuan and Chongqing, 1,394 cells) plus a 90 km disc at Hanzhong (112 cells, inside Cliopatria's shape). Cliopatria's 206 shape also holds Henan and Gansu cells that are not Liu Bang's in 206: the Three Qins fall to him by August or September 205 (Gaozu page) and the Henan front is 204.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 205: 'By August or September 205 BC, the Three Qins and the Guanzhong region had come under Liu's control'; Yin falls in the April-May Henei campaign. Western Wei (Oct-Nov 205) is added from 204, in the next verdict. Revised: Bashu is the Cliopatria Han cells in the Sichuan region (as K0).

correction.text: the Cliopatria Han shape of 206 with the former Western Wei and the former Dai; year 204

keyframe_review.note: 454,874 km2 for 206-204 in Cliopatria's Han row (Sichuan 1121 cells, Henan 377, Shaanxi 313, Chongqing 273, Gansu 166). This is Liu Bang's kingdom, not the Warring States Han. Right for 204 with Western Wei added: Wei Bao 'lost the battle and was captured' in October-November 205, and the Xingyang-Chenggao front of 204 explains the Henan cells. Years 206-205 are the two new keyframes. Revised 2026-10-19: Dai (Zhao Xie's Zhao), which the ledger gives to Han in 205 ('In November 205 BCE, after Han Xin's victory at the Battle of Jingxing', Chu-Han Contention page), is added to the 204 shape; the first draft showed it only in the 203 shape.

1,310,598 km2 for 203: Liu Bang's realm including the lands of the kings he appointed or won (Zhang Er made King of Zhao in 204 'after the Kingdom of Yan had surrendered'; Shandong 831 cells, Hebei 662, Liaoning 406). The pages opened do not date Han Xin's conquest of Qi or the other appointments, so the shape is kept as Cliopatria's and the client lands should be tinted when the Han dynasty's vassal events begin; unverified: page budget. Revised 2026-10-19: Yan is taken out of the direct shape and recorded as a vassal (L8/L9 below): Zang Tu page: 204 'Han Xin sent a messenger to Zang Tu, asking him to pledge allegiance to Liu Bang. Zang Tu agreed'; 202 'Zang Tu became a vassal of the Han Empire and retained his kingly title and territories'. Qi and Zhao stay in the shape as Cliopatria draws them (client kings; han-dynasty should open their vassal events).

region.text: Liu Bang's kingdom at its grant in 206: 'Sichuan, Chongqing, southern Shaanxi' (Eighteen Kingdoms)

ledger.note: 206: Xiang Yu makes Liu Bang King of Han in Bashu and Hanzhong. 'created by military leader Xiang Yu in 206 BCE'; the table: Hàn (漢), Liu Bang, 'Sichuan, Chongqing, southern Shaanxi'. The Gaozu page dates the title to the second month of the first year of his reign.

205: Liu Bang takes the Yong kingdom, 'central Shaanxi, and eastern Gansu'. 'By August or September 205 BC, the Three Qins and the Guanzhong region had come under Liu's control.' The kingdom's land is the Eighteen Kingdoms table's.
205: Liu Bang takes the Sai kingdom, 'northeastern Shaanxi' (same sentence as Yong).
205: Liu Bang takes the Di (Zhai) kingdom, 'northern Shaanxi' (same sentence as Yong). The disc at Yulin, Shaanxi is the researcher's reading of 'northern Shaanxi'.

205: Han Xin captures Wei Bao and Western Wei falls. 'In October-November 205 BCE, Wei Bao personally led an attack on Han Xin but lost the battle and was captured'; the Wei Bao page: Western Wei became Hedong Commandery. Wei Bao had defected to Chu earlier that year.

region.text: Zhao Xie's Zhao (Dai): 'northern Shanxi, northwestern Hebei'

ledger.note: 205: Han Xin's army defeats Zhao Xie's Zhao (Dai) after Chen Yu's seizure of Changshan; in November 205 'Han Xin's victory at the Battle of Jingxing'. The Eighteen Kingdoms table: Zhao (Dai), 'Lost to Liu Bang', 'northern Shanxi, northwestern Hebei'. The year is the page's for the Jingxing sentence; the fall of Dai itself is undated there.

April 205: Liu Bang attacks Henei with Wei Bao's help. 'In April-May 205 BCE, Liu Bang attacked Henei with help from Wei Bao, the King of Western Wei.' Henei is placed on Yin, 'northern Henan, southern Hebei' (table).

204: the Xingyang-Chenggao standoff with Xiang Yu begins. 'In 204 BCE, after sustaining losses from Chu attacks on his supply routes to Xingyang, Liu Bang's forces ran short of supplies'; the Wei Bao page: 'In 204 BC, during the Battle of Xingyang, Liu Bang left Wei Bao to defend Xingyang.'

region.text: Zang Tu's Yan (Cliopatria's Yan shape of 204)

ledger.note: 204: Yan comes under Han. Zang Tu page: 'Han Xin sent a messenger to Zang Tu, asking him to pledge allegiance to Liu Bang. Zang Tu agreed.' The Chu-Han Contention page dates the surrender of the Kingdom of Yan to 204 ('In 204 BCE, after the Kingdom of Yan had surrendered to him, Liu Bang made Zhang Er the new King of Zhao'). Zang Tu keeps his kingship, so Yan is a vassal, not a gain; the year is the pages', the extent is Cliopatria's Yan shape (confidence 2). Replaces the first draft's 203 'gain' of Yan (confidence 1, Cliopatria's year).

region.text: the part of Cliopatria's 203 Han shape that is Qi's 204 shape

ledger.note: 203: Cliopatria's 203 Han shape holds the Qi lands; no page opened dates Han Xin's conquest of Qi (page silent).

region.text: Zang Tu's Yan (Cliopatria's Yan shape of 204)

ledger.note: 203: end of this dossier, not of the relation. Zang Tu page: in 202 'Zang Tu became a vassal of the Han Empire and retained his kingly title and territories', rebelled in about August 202 and was captured and executed; the han-dynasty dossier carries the Yan vassalage from 202 to the revolt. Paired here only because the Kingdom of Han ends in 203. [fx-39, R009: moved from 203 to 28 February 202 with the end of the dossier, which now runs to Liu Bang's proclamation as emperor.]

203: Liu Bang renounces the peace with Chu. 'In 203 BCE, while Xiang Yu was retreating eastwards, Liu Bang ... renounced the peace agreement'; the Hong Canal treaty is undated on the page and the fighting resumes until Gaixia (202). [fx-39, R009: moved from 203 to 28 February 202 with the end of the dossier, which now runs to Liu Bang's proclamation as emperor.]

region.text: the realm handed to the Han dynasty row

ledger.note: 28 February 202 BC: Liu Bang's time as King of Han runs from c. March 206 to 28 February 202 BC, when he becomes emperor ('In 202 BC, Liu became emperor with the support of his subjects'; the regnal table marks the King of Han title 'Merged in the Crown'), and the Kingdom of Han continues as the Han dynasty. Moved from 203 in fx-39 (R009): Cliopatria's Han row ends in 203, but the Xin of Han page has Han Xin 'a vassal of the Hàn Empire after Liu Bang defeated Xiang Yu in 202 BC' and the empire dates from 202, so ending the dossier in 203 handed the realm to han-dynasty a year before that dossier starts.

wars.name: Han conquest of the Three Qins
wars.outcome: Liu Bang took the Three Qins and Guanzhong by August or September 205.

wars.name: Han Xin's campaigns against Wei and Zhao
wars.outcome: Wei Bao was captured in October-November 205; Han Xin then defeated Chen Yu's Zhao at Jingxing (November 205).

wars.name: Chu-Han Contention
wars.outcome: A war between Liu Bang and Xiang Yu between the fall of Qin (206) and the Han dynasty (202): Pengcheng fell to a coalition under Liu Bang in September-October 205 and was retaken by Chu; the 204 standoff at Xingyang; the Hong Canal treaty renounced in 203; Gaixia in 202.
wars.note: Only 206-203 is this dossier's; the Han dynasty dossier takes up 202.

certainty.note: Frontiers with Western Chu, Zhao, Yan and Qi were set by campaigns and enfeoffments, not surveys; the 203 realm includes client kingdoms.

notes:
New dossier: a split of Cliopatria's 'Han' row. The row's shapes 206-204 and 203 are Liu Bang's Kingdom of Han (Hàn 漢), not the Warring States Han (韓), which is dossier han (reviews the 404-208 shapes). The Han dynasty (han-dynasty, ea-02) is the same state from 202; Cliopatria's Han row ends in 203 and the Han Dynasty row begins in 202. Pages opened: Eighteen Kingdoms, Chu-Han Contention, Emperor Gaozu of Han, Wei Bao. Not on the pages: the month of the 206 title (the footnote gives the second month of Gaozu's first year, a Chinese-calendar month), Hanzhong or Nanzheng as a capital, the Hong Canal treaty's date, Han Xin's conquests of Yan and Qi, Zhang Er's appointment beyond 'In 204 BCE ... Liu Bang made Zhang Er the new King of Zhao', the vassal status of Zhao, Yan and Qi (the han-dynasty dossier should open vassal events from 202). Wikidata: none for this split; Cliopatria's Q1968654 belongs to the Warring States Han. 'wikipedia' is the Han dynasty article, the nearest page. Counterparts yong, sai, zhai, yin, dai and chang-shan are ea-02 slugs; western-chu is ea-02's; 'Zhao (Zhang Er)' has no dossier.

Revision 2026-10-19 (after review ea-01-d). (1) Bashu: {region: 'Sichuan (region)'} is replaced by the Cliopatria Han 206 cells inside it (1,394) plus the Hanzhong disc, in K0, K1, L0 and the predecessor land; the 740 plateau cells west of 102.5 E are gone and the K0 note's area statement is corrected (Cliopatria's 206 shape is not 'far larger'; it is larger than the grant only by Henan and Gansu cells). (2) Dai is in the 204 keyframe. (3) Yan: the 203 'gain' is replaced by a vassal_start in 204 (confidence 2) and a vassal_end in 203 (the dossier's last year; the relation continues under han-dynasty until Zang Tu's revolt in 202), and the 203 keyframe takes Yan out of the direct shape; Zang Tu page: he 'retained his kingly title and territories'. The yan dossier (another part) ends 202 and has no matching vassal event: mirror it as Yan a vassal of kingdom-of-han from 204. (4) Orchestrator decision still open: the dossier says the Kingdom of Han and the Han dynasty are one state under a new title, and rule 2 would fold 206-203 into han-dynasty (ea-02) as a rename in 202 (two dossiers changing colour in 202 otherwise); I did not merge, because the split was made on Cliopatria's 'Han' row and han-dynasty is another group's file. (5) Not done: Han Xin's conquest of Qi remains undated (Chu-Han page: the Wei River passage is late 204 with no exact date; the request to be made king of Qi is undated), so the 203 Qi gain stays Cliopatria's (confidence 1).
